articles.title: Swiss AI Startup Prem Is Raising $100 Million Series A Round
articles.summary: Prem AI, a Swiss startup that helps companies including hedge funds and law firms run artificial intelligence models on their own private infrastructure, is raising $100 million in a Series A funding round.
articles.author: Natalia Kniazhevich

articles.title: AI Company Dream Triples Value to $3 Billion in Funding Round
articles.summary: Dream, an Israeli artificial intelligence company that provides AI and cybersecurity services to governments and critical infrastructure operators, has raised $260 million at a $3 billion valuation.
articles.author: Galit Altstein

articles.title: Stocks Fall as Traders See Fed Hike by October | The Close 6/17/2026
articles.summary: Bloomberg Television brings you the latest news and analysis leading up to the final minutes and seconds before and after the closing bell on Wall Street. Today's guests are DoubleLine Capital Portfolio Manager Ken Shinoda, Former Federal Reserve Vice Chair Alan Blinder, The Conference Board Chief Economist Dana Peterson, Former FDIC Chair Sheila Bair, & Barings’ High Yield Portfolio Manager Kelly Burton. (Source: Bloomberg)

articles.title: Roelof Botha joins SpaceX’s board of directors
articles.summary: The former Sequoia Capital leader is filling an "existing vacancy" on SpaceX's board, days after the company went public in the largest IPO ever.
articles.author: Sean O'Kane

articles.title: Capital Factory CEO Killed in Private-Jet Crash in Texas
articles.summary: Joshua Baer, the founder and chief executive officer of the venture capital firm Capital Factory, died Tuesday in a plane crash in South Texas, the Austin American-Statesman reported.
articles.author: Madlin Mekelburg, Kara Carlson

articles.title: Only 16 percent of Americans think AI will have a positive impact on society, a new study shows
articles.summary: Although Wall Street loves AI, every day Americans are significantly less optimistic about the industry, a new report from Pew Research shows.
articles.author: Lucas Ropek

articles.title: SpaceX Adds $1 Trillion in Value Since IPO
articles.summary: SpaceX has rapidly added $1 trillion in market capitalization since its recent public debut, reaching approximately $2.7 trillion and positioning itself as the fifth largest company globally, close to overtaking Microsoft. Mandeep Singh has more on "Bloomberg Open Interest." (Source: Bloomberg)

articles.title: Goldman's Kaplan on Fed's Warsh and AI Capex Boom
articles.summary: Robert Kaplan, Goldman Sachs vice chair and former Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas president, expects Federal Reserve's Kevin Warsh to adopt a more neutral tone in his first news conference as chair. Speaking on "Bloomberg Open Interest," Kaplan also says he sees an "historic" capital expenditures boom in the US. (Source: Bloomberg)

articles.title: JPMorgan’s David Kelly Says AI Boom Will Refuel Stock Rally
articles.summary: JPMorgan Chase & Co.’s asset-management arm is urging investors to stick with stocks and other higher-risk assets in the second half of 2026, arguing that an AI investment boom and resilient consumers should keep the expansion intact despite persistent inflation and a Federal Reserve on hold.
articles.author: Isabelle Lee

articles.title: SoftBank Scales Back Latin America Tech Bets as Venture Capital Boom Fades
articles.summary: SoftBank Group Corp. is struggling to find startups in Latin America ready for major investments, underscoring how sharply the tech boom there has cooled since attracting record levels of venture capital only a few years ago.
articles.author: Giovanna Bellotti Azevedo, Zijia Song

articles.title: Brookfield-Backed Data Center Firm Csquare Files for US IPO
articles.summary: Csquare Inc., a data center company backed by Brookfield Corp., filed publicly for a US initial public offering, joining a rush of debuts linked to artificial intelligence infrastructure.
articles.author: Anthony Hughes

articles.title: SpaceX bets $60 billion on Cursor to catch OpenAI and Anthropic
articles.summary: Just two trading days after its IPO, Elon Musk's SpaceX is buying AI coding startup Anysphere. The deal is meant to help the struggling xAI division catch up with Anthropic and OpenAI. The article SpaceX bets $60 billion on Cursor to catch OpenAI and Anthropic appeared first on The Decoder.
articles.author: Maximilian Schreiner

articles.title: AI Can Play 'Significant' Role in Tech for Managing Diabetes, Says David Roman
articles.summary: David Roman, US medtech and healthcare IT research analyst for Goldman Sachs, said that AI play a 'significant' role in helping patients stay on top of their diabetes, with companies like Abbott and Dexcom using new technology to count carbohydrates and deliver the right amount of insulin. Roman, joined by Bloomberg health reporter Madison Muller, said that he came away from Goldman Sach's annual medtech conference 'very bullish' on innovation across the industry. (Source: Bloomberg)

articles.title: SpaceX Investor Powerlaw Debuts Amid IPO Race
articles.summary: Powerlaw, a closed-end fund that owns stakes in Elon Musk’s SpaceX and artificial intelligence firm OpenAI, traded well above the value of its underlying investments in its debut, capitalizing on retail investors’ clamor for exposure to the hottest private tech companies. Bloomberg's Anthony Hughes and Mike Dinsdale, CEO at Powerlaw join to discuss Powerlaw’s platform allowing exposure to private tech companies as well as the IPO enviroment. (Source: Bloomberg)

articles.title: DeepSeek takes outside money for the first time at a $50 billion valuation
articles.summary: Chinese AI startup DeepSeek has raised more than 50 billion yuan - about $7.4 billion - in its first external funding round. The article DeepSeek takes outside money for the first time at a $50 billion valuation appeared first on The Decoder.
articles.author: Jonathan Kemper

articles.title: Dan Ives on US-Anthropic Talks, AI M&A, Open AI Losses
articles.summary: Dan Ives, global senior equity analyst at Wedbush Securities, discusses what he calls the “tug of war” between Anthropic and the Trump administration, why he expects accelerated M&A on artificial intelligence, and reported losses at OpenAI ahead of the company’s IPO later this year. (Source: Bloomberg)

articles.title: SpaceX to acquire Cursor for $60B in stock, days after blockbuster IPO
articles.summary: The deal is supposed to help SpaceX's struggling AI division. The company told IPO investors it sees a $26 trillion addressable market in AI.
articles.author: Sean O'Kane

articles.title: ‘This System Wasn’t Built For Me’: Black Founders Became Investors To Change Venture Capital
articles.summary: The consistently low numbers of U.S. venture funding to Black founders led some to turn to investing in an effort to help level the playing field. Crunchbase News talked with two such founders to hear more about their experiences in raising capital and what they’ve learned from investing.
articles.author: Judy Rider

articles.title: Will it take a ‘Chernobyl-scale disaster’ for us to regulate cyber weapons of mass destruction? | Stuart Russell
articles.summary: Unrestrained development of unsafe AI systems is leading to intolerable risksStuart Russell is a computer scientist known for his contributions to AI and a new Guardian US columnistThe AI company Anthropic has been making major headlines recently. Its trillion-dollar IPO plan and its blood feud with secretary of defense Pete Hegseth have attracted much attention, but two other events may be even more consequential.In early June, the company posted an article describing early signs of recursive self-improvement (RSI), a process in which an AI system devises ways to increase its own intelligence, leading to a greater ability to improve itself, and so on.Stuart Russell is a distinguished professor of computer science at University of California, Berkeley, the president of the International Association for Safe and Ethical Artificial Intelligence and a Guardian US columnist Continue reading...
articles.author: Stuart Russell

articles.title: China's AI Markets Still 'A Source of Funds' Says Citigroup
articles.summary: Alicia Yap, Citi's head of Pan-Asia Internet Research, breaks down where China's tech market stands amid global AI adoption. But despite all this heavy corporate activity, Citigroup warns that global investors are still treating China tech as "a source of funds," with Wall Street dumping local stocks to fund the global AI hardware trade. She joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

articles.title: SpaceX Stocks Still Volatile, Says JPMorgan Strategist
articles.summary: Stephanie Aliaga, JPMorgan Asset Management global market strategist, says to expect SpaceX volatility in the next six months. She also says they are expective some big high-profile AI names, but the IPO markets are still going to be selective. She joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

articles.title: Chainguard, Cyber Firms Use AI to Hunt for Open-Source Flaws
articles.summary: More than two dozen companies including JPMorgan Chase & Co. and an array of cybersecurity firms are collaborating to remedy software flaws spotted by cutting-edge artificial intelligence models.
articles.author: Rachel Metz
